thread:
evan: publish blocked — CI failing on release step. changelog-semver-lint flagged a bump but nothing in changelog. publishflow says "version mismatch". anyone seen this with recent codegen changes?
ci-bot: publishflow-ci: step failed: changelog-lint
ci-bot: logs: "Detected semver bump in package @redwood/sample-app: 1.2.3 -> 1.3.0 but no changelog entry found"
lena: :eyes: I just rebased the OpenAPI generator change that stabilizes parameter ordering. Could that reorder cause the package manifest to detect ABI changes?
ev an: maybe — type-hash for TS SDK changed which triggers our semver checker. I ran `yarn regen:types` locally and got diffs.
ev an: failing snippet:
```
- export type Foo = { bar?: string }
+ export type Foo = { bar?: string; baz?: number }
```
sam: that looks like a real type addition; changelog should have been bumped. But commit history only shows whitespace / ordering changes in codegen templates.
marta: Could a reorder of optional params make the type comparator think it's an added field? Our comparator is naive.
jon: We had a similar comparator bug last year — it treats reordering as an additive change when optional fields move after a required one.
lena: Repro steps I used:
```
git checkout main
git pull
yarn run tools/codegen --openapi=./specs/main.yaml
yarn regen:types
git diff -- package/sdk
```
sam: quick fix: revert the stable-sort commit in the codegen template and re-run regen to produce parity. But we need a longer fix — update semver-lint to ignore pure reorders and only flag real additions.
ev an: I'll open a tiny PR that patches the comparator and adds a unit test. In the meantime, I'll backport a revert so we can unblock the publish.
marta: tag me on the PR, I'll validate sampleapp onboarding flow.
jon: re-run CI after the revert: `ci-bot re-run 1718675300` :thumbsup:
ci-bot: CI queued — publishflow-lint now green on branch evan/codegen-ordering-hotfix :sparkles:
ev an: rolling the backport + comparator PRs now. thanks all :heart:
sam: long-term: add a pre-publish regen check in CI that diffs generated SDKs and uploads the result to the release ticket. saves surprises.
lena: also logging the regen hash in build metadata would help trace these bumps quickly.
ev an: agreed. I'll include both follow-ups in the comparator PR.
